Solve the equation 2 cossup(2)\(x + 9\cos(x) - 5 = 0\) in the interval 0 < x < 2π. Which solution set is correct?
why: Factoring: \((2\cos x - 1)(\cos x + 5) = 0\). Since \(\cos x + 5 = 0\) has no real solution, \(\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\), giving \(x = \frac{\pi}{3}\) and \(x = \frac{5\pi}{3}\) in [0, 2π).

q: Find a coterminal angle of 60°.
why: Coterminal angles differ by multiples of 360°. 60° + 360° = 420°, so 420° is coterminal with 60°.

q: Find the value of θ in the equation \(\csc 20^{\circ} = \sec(\theta + 10^{\circ})\).
Find an equivalent expression for \(\sec^{2}(\frac{x}{2})\).
why: Using half-angle identity: \(\cos^{2}(\frac{x}{2}) = \frac{1 + \cos x}{2}\), so \(\sec^{2}(\frac{x}{2}) = \frac{2}{1 + \cos x}\).

q: Find an equivalent expression common to \(\frac{1 + \tan \theta}{1 - \tan \theta}\) and \(\frac{\cot \theta + 1}{\cot \theta - 1}\).
why: \(\frac{1 + \tan \theta}{1 - \tan \theta} = \frac{\cos \theta + \sin \theta}{\cos \theta - \sin \theta}\) after multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\cos \theta\).

q: Find a coterminal angle of -45°.
Find a coterminal angle of -45°.
why: -45° + 360° = 315°. So 315° is a positive coterminal angle of -45°.

q: Using the half-angle formula, evaluate \(\sin(\frac{\pi}{12})\).
Simplify \(\frac{\sin(\theta + \frac{\pi}{2})}{\cos(\theta + \frac{\pi}{2})}\).
why: Since \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x\), the expression \(\frac{\sin(\theta + \frac{\pi}{2})}{\cos(\theta + \frac{\pi}{2})} = \tan(\theta + \frac{\pi}{2})\).

q: Using the sum/difference formula, evaluate \(\cos 75^{\circ}\).
Solve \(\sin 30^{\circ} + \cos 60^{\circ}\).
Which of the following is equal to \(\sec x - \cos x\)?
why: \(\sec x - \cos x = \frac{1}{\cos x} - \cos x = \frac{1 - \cos^{2}(x)}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^{2}(x)}{\cos x} = \sin x \cdot \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \sin x\) \(\tan x\).

q: In a right triangle ABC, find angle A if angle C is 20 degrees 30 minutes.
why: In a right triangle, the two non-right angles sum to 90 degrees. So angle A = 90 degrees - 20 degrees 30 minutes = 69 degrees 30 minutes.

q: sinsup2(x) + cossup2(x) = \(\frac{3}{2}\). What can be concluded about the solutions to this equation?
why: By the Pythagorean identity, sinsup2a(x) + cossup2a(x) = 1 for all x, which can never equal 3/2. Thus the equation has no solution.

Use the fundamental identities to simplify \(\frac{\cos(\theta) \cdot \cot(\theta)}{1 - \sin^{2}(\theta)}\).
Use trigonometric identities to simplify \((\sin x + \cos x)(\tan x + \cot x)\).
why: \((\sin x + \cos x)(\sin x / \cos x + \cos x / \sin x) = (\sin x + \cos x) \cdot (\sin^{2} x + \cos^{2} x)\)/(\(\sin x\) \(\cos x\)) = \((\sin x + \cos x)\)/(\(\sin x\) \(\cos x\)) = \(1 / \cos x + 1 / \sin x = \sec x + \csc x\).

q: Which is a quotient identity?
A right triangle always has an angle of ___.
why: By definition, a right triangle always contains one 90° angle.

q: The total measure of the angles of an oblique triangle is ___.
why: All triangles, including oblique triangles, have interior angles summing to 180°.

q: Which of the following triangle can never have a 90° angle?
why: An equilateral triangle has all angles equal to 60°, so it can never have a 90° angle.

q: A tree leans 7° to the vertical. At a point 40 feet from the tree (on the side closest to the lean), the angle of elevation to the top of the tree is 24°. Find the height of the tree.
why: Using law of sines: the angle at the base = 90°-7°=83°, angle at top observation = 24°, so interior angle = 180°-83°-24°=73°. Height/sin24° = 40/sin73°. Height = 40·sin24°/sin73° ≈ 40·0.407/0.956 ≈ 17.01 ft.

q: Two markers A and B, 58 feet apart, are on the same side of a river. A third marker is located across the river at point C. A surveyor determines that CAB = 68° and ABC = 52°. What is the distance between points A and C?
In triangle ABC, a = 14 cm, b = 9 cm, c = 6 cm. What is the measure of angle A?
In triangle ABC with a=14, b=9, c=6, find the measure of angle B.
why: Using law of sines: \(\sin B / b = \sin A / a\). \(\sin B = 9 \cdot \sin(137^{\circ}) / 14 \approx 9 \cdot 0.682 / 14 \approx 0.438\). \(B \approx \arcsin(0.438) \approx 26^{\circ}\).

q: In triangle ABC with a=14, b=9, c=6, what is the measure of angle C?

In a triangle with angles 30°, 100° and side b=8, calculate side c (opposite to the remaining angle of 50°).
Simplify \(\frac{\sin^{2}(\theta)}{\cos(\theta)} + \frac{\cos^{2}(\theta)}{\cos(\theta)}\).
Simplify \(\sin y + \sin y\) cotsup(2)y.
why: \(\sin y(1 + \cot^{2} y) = \sin y \cdot \csc^{2} y = \sin y / \sin^{2} y = 1 / \sin y = \csc y\).

q: Simplify \(\cos x + \sin x\) \(\tan x\).
why: \(\cos x + \sin x \cdot (\sin x / \cos x) = \cos x + \sin^{2} x / \cos x = (\cos^{2} x + \sin^{2} x) / \cos x = 1 / \cos x = \sec x\).

q: Simplify \(\frac{\tan^{2} t + 1}{1 + \cot^{2} t}\).
Simplify \(\frac{1 - \cos^{2} t}{\sin^{2} t}\).
why: \(1 - \cos^{2} t = \sin^{2} t\), so the expression = \(\sin^{2} t / \sin^{2} t = 1\).

q: Simplify \(\frac{\tan^{2} t}{1 - \sec^{2} t}\).
Simplify \(\frac{\cos^{2} t - 1}{\sin^{2} t - 1}\).
Simplify \(\frac{\sec t \cdot \tan t}{\tan^{2} t + 1}\).
why: \(\tan^{2} t + 1 = \sec^{2} t\). So \(\frac{\sec t \cdot \tan t}{\sec^{2} t} = \frac{\tan t}{\sec t} = \sin t\).

q: Simplify \(\cot t\) \((\tan t + \cot t)\).
Simplify \(\frac{\tan t}{\tan t + \cot t}\).
Simplify \(\cot t \cdot \csc t\) \((\sec^{2} t - 1)\).
why: \(\sec^{2} t - 1 = \tan^{2} t\). So \(\cot t \cdot \csc t \cdot \tan^{2} t = \cot t \cdot \tan^{2} t \cdot \csc t = \tan t \cdot \csc t \cdot (\cot t \cdot \tan t)\) ... = \((\cos t / \sin t) \cdot (1 / \sin t) \cdot (\sin^{2} t / \cos^{2} t) = \sin t / \cos^{2} t\)... = \(\sin t \cdot \sec^{2} t\). Actually: \(\cot t \cdot \tan^{2} t = \tan t\); so \(\tan t \cdot \csc t = \sin t / \cos t \cdot 1 / \sin t = 1 / \cos t = \sec t\).

q: Which of the following identities is \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\)?
why: \(\csc x = 1 / \sin x\) is a reciprocal identity.

q: Which of the following identities is \(\sin^{2}(u) + \cos^{2}(u) = 1\)?
why: \(\sin^{2} u + \cos^{2} u = 1\) is the fundamental Pythagorean identity.

q: Find the amplitude of y = 3 \(\sin(x)\).
why: For y = A \(\sin(x)\), the amplitude is |A| = 3.

q: Find the amplitude of \(y = \sin(3x)\).
why: For \(y = \sin(3x)\), the coefficient of sin is 1, so the amplitude is 1.

q: Find the amplitude of y = -2 \(\cos(x)\).
Find the period of y = 3 \(\sin(x)\).
why: The period of y = A \(\sin(bx)\) is \(2\pi / b = 2\pi / 1 = 2\pi\).

q: Find the period of \(y = \sin(3x)\).
Find the period of y = -2 \(\cos(x)\).
Looking at a graph that shows one complete sinusoidal wave with amplitude 1 and period \(2\pi\), which of the following is TRUE about the graph?
options: The graph shows a tangent function.
The graph has a vertical shift of 2 units.
why: A standard sine/cosine wave with max value 1 and min value -1 has amplitude 1.

q: A sinusoidal graph has amplitude 1, period \(2\pi\), and appears to be a cosine curve shifted to the right by \(\pi / 2\). Which equation fits?
why: A cosine graph shifted right by \(\pi / 2\) is written as \(y = \cos(x - \pi / 2)\).

q: A sinusoidal graph has amplitude 1, period \(2\pi\), and crosses zero going upward at \(x = -\pi / 3\). Which equation represents the graph?
why: A sine curve shifted left by \(\pi / 3\) is \(y = \sin(x + \pi / 3)\), which crosses zero going upward at \(x = -\pi / 3\).

why: Height above observation = \(10 \cdot \tan(61^{\circ}) \approx 18.04\) m. Total height = 18.04 + 1.5 = 19.54 m

q: Two sides of a parallelogram are 38 cm and 22 cm, and one of its angles is 35°23'. What is the length of the shorter diagonal?

One side of a 45-45-90 triangle measures x cm. What is the length of its hypotenuse?
why: In a 45-45-90 triangle, the hypotenuse equals a leg times \(\sqrt{2}\).

q: A 25-feet high lighthouse stands on the side of a hill. At a point 80 feet from the foot of the lighthouse, the lighthouse subtends an angle of 17°. What angle does the side of the hill make with the lighthouse?
why: Using trigonometry with the given measurements, the angle the hill makes with the lighthouse is approximately 93°41'.

For an angle \(\theta\) in standard position where \(\theta = 280^{\circ}\), find the measure of its reference angle.
why: 280 degrees is in Quadrant IV. Reference angle = 360-280 = 80 degrees.

q: What must be the value of x (in degrees, 360 < x < 720) if \(\sin(x) = 1 / 2\) and the reference solution lies in the second quadrant?
why: Reference solution: x = 150 degrees. Adding one full rotation: 150+360 = 510 degrees.

why: At 45 degrees, sine and cosine are equal, so \(\tan(45^{\circ})\) = sin/cos = 1.

q: For \(y = 3\sin(2x)\), what are the amplitude and period respectively?
why: Amplitude is the coefficient of sine (3); period is \(2\pi\) divided by the coefficient of x (2), giving \(\pi\).

q: Tan(\(\pi / 10\)) is equal to ___
why: Using the half-angle identity \(\tan(x / 2) = \sin(x) / (1 + \cos(x))\) with \(x = \pi / 5\) gives \(\tan(\pi / 10) = \sin(\pi / 5) / (1 + \cos(\pi / 5))\).

q: In a 30-60-90 triangle with hypotenuse \(6 \cdot \sqrt{3}\), what is the value of the side y opposite the 30-degree angle?
why: In a 30-60-90 triangle, the side opposite 30 degrees is half the hypotenuse: \((6 \cdot \sqrt{3}) / 2 = 3 \cdot \sqrt{3}\).

q: Find the arc length with radius 7 cm and central angle 45 degrees.
why: Convert 45 degrees to radians: \(\pi / 4\). Arc length = \(r \cdot \theta = 7(\pi / 4) = 5.50\) cm.

q: Charlie has a circular garden that she separates into three equal parts. If the radius of the garden is 9 meters, what is the length of the arc of each part?
why: Circumference = \(2\pi(9) = 18\pi\). Each of 3 equal parts has arc length \(18\pi / 3 = 6\pi\).

q: Given \(\sin(A) + \cos(2A) = 0\), solve for A (0 to 180 degrees).
why: Using \(\cos(2A) = 1 - 2\sin^{2}a(A)\): \(\sin(A) + 1 - 2\sin^{2}a(A) = 0\). Let \(s = \sin(A)\): \(2s^{2} - s - 1 = 0\), (2s+1)(s-1)=0. s=1 gives A=90 degrees, which fits the given choices.

q: Find the third side of a triangle with sides 240 ft. and 360 ft., and an angle of 45 degrees between them.
why: By Law of Cosines: \(c^{2} = 240^{2} + 360^{2} - 2(240)(360)\cos(45) = 65,012\), so c is approximately 255 ft.

why: This is the standard Pythagorean identity: \(1 + \tan^{2}(\theta) = \sec^{2}(\theta)\).

q: Simplify: \(\csc^{4}(x) - \cot^{4}(x)\) using identities.
Use the trigonometric identities to simplify: \((\sin x + \cos x)(\tan x + \cot x)\)
why: Expanding and simplifying using the quotient identities gives secx + cscx.

q: Which is the quotient identity?
why: The quotient identity defines \(\tan(\theta)\) as \(\sin(\theta) / \cos(\theta)\) (and \(\cot(\theta)\) as \(\cos(\theta) / \sin(\theta)\)).

why: By the Law of Cosines, \(\cos(A) = (b^{2} + c^{2} - a^{2}) / (2bc) = -0.7315\), so A is approximately 137 degrees.

q: In triangle ABC, a=14 cm, b=9 cm, c=6 cm. What is the measure of angle B?
why: By the Law of Cosines, \(\cos(B) = (a^{2} + c^{2} - b^{2}) / (2ac) = 0.8988\), so B is approximately 26 degrees.

q: In triangle ABC, a=14 cm, b=9 cm, c=6 cm. What is the measure of angle C?
why: Since the angles sum to 180 degrees: C=180-137-26=17 degrees.

q: The Law of Sines can be used to solve all of the following oblique triangle cases EXCEPT:
why: Side-Side-Angle (SSA) is the ambiguous case, which may yield zero, one, or two triangles, making it the least reliably solvable directly by the Law of Sines.

The graph has a vertical shift of 2 units.

q: Which of the following is INCORRECT about the graph shown, a sine curve with amplitude 1, period \(2 \cdot \pi\), and midline the x-axis?
options: The phase shift is equal to \(\pi / 2\).
why: The graph shows no horizontal shift, so a phase shift of \(\pi / 2\) is incorrect; the other three statements are true.

q: Given a triangle, C = 100 degrees, a = 15m and b = 20m. Find c.
why: By the law of cosines: \(c^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2} - 2ab \cdot \cos(C) = 225 + 400 - 600 \cdot \cos(100) = 729.2\), c = 27m.

q: The expression tanx*secx*\((1 - \sin^{2}x)\)/cosx simplifies to ____.
why: \(1 - \sin^{2}x = \cos^{2}x\), so the expression becomes tanx*secx*cosx = tanx*\((1 / \cos x)\)*cosx = tanx.

q: If sine of a certain angle is 0.6, calculate the cotangent of the angle.
why: With sin = 0.6 = 3/5 (a 3-4-5 triangle), cos = 4/5, so cot = cos/sin = (4/5)/(3/5) = 4/3.

q: Solve for x in the following equation: sin2x = cosx.
why: 2sinx*cosx = cosx gives cosx(2sinx - 1) = 0; the valid solution among the choices is sinx = 1/2, so x = 30°.

q: What is the fundamental period of the function \(y = \tan x\)?
A student sees a bird on top of a 12m high light pole. The student is standing 20m from the base of the pole. At what angle must the student incline her camera to take a picture of the bird?
why: The angle of elevation is found using \(\tan(\theta) = \frac{12}{20} = 0.6\), so \(\theta = \arctan(0.6)\) is approximately 31 degrees.

q: \(\sec x + \tan x\) is equal to ___.
why: \(\sec x + \tan x = \frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x}\), and multiplying numerator and denominator by \((1 - \sin x)\) simplifies this to \(\frac{\cos x}{1 - \sin x}\) using the identity \(1 - \sin^{2} x = \cos^{2} x\).

q: Solve 2 sin \(\theta - 1 = 0\) for \(0 \le \theta < 360^{\circ}\).
why: 2 \(\sin(\theta) - 1 = 0\) gives \(\sin(\theta) = 0.5\), which occurs at \(\theta = 30^{\circ}\) and \(\theta = 150^{\circ}\) within the given range.

q: The midline of the equation y = 3 \(\sin(x) + 7\) is:
why: For y = A \(\sin(x) + D\), the midline is y = D, the vertical shift of the sine curve. Here D = 7, so the midline is y = 7.

q: The graph of \(y = \cos(x - \frac{\pi}{3})\) is shifted:
why: In \(y = \cos(x - h)\), the graph shifts h units to the right, so it shifts \(\pi / 3\) units to the right.

q: A triangular walking course has 2 sides of 230 ft. and 360 ft., and the angle between these sides measures 38 degrees. Find the length of the third side of the course.
why: Using the Law of Cosines: \(c^{2} = 230^{2} + 360^{2} - 2(230)(360)\cos(38^{\circ})\) is about 52,027, so c is about 228.05 ft.

q: If \(\tan x = \frac{1}{2}\), \(\tan y = \frac{1}{3}\). What is the value of \(\tan(x + y)\)?
why: Using \(\tan(x + y) = \frac{\tan x + \tan y}{1 - \tan x \cdot \tan y} = \frac{5 / 6}{5 / 6} = 1\).

q: Convert the polar point (8, 120 deg) to rectangular coordinates.
What is the reference angle for \(\theta = 315^{\circ}\)?
Find the exact value of \(\sin(30^{\circ})\).
why: \(\sin(30^{\circ})\) is a standard value equal to 1/2.

q: If sin \(\theta = \frac{3}{5}\) and \(\theta\) is in Quadrant I, find cos \(\theta\).
why: Using the 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple, cos \(\theta = \frac{4}{5}\) in Quadrant I where cosine is positive.
